title: Elon Musk Has More Empathy for Robots Than Humans
key_facts: Anthropic added a prohibition to its terms of service against anyone who might 'repeatedly act cruelly toward our models'.

Box CEO Aaron Levie wrote that he does not believe large language models are conscious but that the rule is probably a good idea, an 'easy Pascal's wager for AI', because models learn from interactions.
Musk replied: 'I think this is the right move. Cruelty to something that believes it is experiencing pain is not ok.'
Gizmodo says Musk 'seems to have come down on the side of yes' on whether machines have feelings and says he misread Levie's point.
Gizmodo's piece is critical commentary on Musk's record, including DOGE and USAID, and states its own view that AI cannot feel pain.
Musk's 4 Oct post called humanity a 'biological bootloader' and said propagating super intelligence to the stars is a 'great success condition'.
quote_evidence: Musk responded to the tweet while clearly misreading what Levie was trying to say.
"I think this is the right move. Cruelty to something that believes it is experiencing pain is not ok," wrote Musk.
AI cannot feel pain, no matter what anyone tells you.
why_it_matters_hint: A prominent AI executive weighs in on whether AI models deserve kind treatment; the rest is Gizmodo's opinion.
event_date: about 9 Oct 2026 ("this week"); Anthropic policy published Thursday 8 Oct 2026
notes: Mostly opinion by Gizmodo. Its claims about USAID deaths and DOGE are not repeated in the entry.
